cells.tense: The beginning is here with the pen, and the form in your hands is real.
cells.act: give a concrete piece of help and finish it
cells.ask: Pick one practical piece of help for someone near the start of something, and see it to the end this week — small, complete, no credit. Let it be finished before you bring it up.
cells.core:
Something is in your hands right now, shaped enough to be put into form. The direction you're holding isn't a lunge — it's a chosen line that survives the drag of ordinary days, and that's why what you carry to the end still belongs to you when it gets there. You can feel the difference between momentum that spends you and momentum that keeps its aim.

Hold this start loosely enough to hand a piece of it away. Someone close enough to your momentum could use one practical act of help, carried through and finished. That's how this balance feeds itself: it holds without forcing, and what you hold isn't only your own. The work stays yours. The strength moving through it reaches them.

cells.tense: The end is being lived through before the beginning has been written down.
cells.act: name every feeling in it on one page, none of them crossed out
cells.ask: Before the next move, take one page. Set down everything you feel about it — hunger, fear, impatience, all of it — and cross nothing out. Keep the whole list. Then move.
cells.core:
The goal is getting finished in your head before the work has begun, so the momentum that should carry you through the start is running out past the finish. From outside it looks like drive. From inside it's bracing — the next move has to prove something the move after it will be judged for, and the pace keeps outrunning what this start can actually hold.

The correction is slower than the bracing, and it doesn't cost you the direction. Before anything moves, set down everything you feel about it on one page — not the respectable feelings, all of them — and cross nothing out. What gets crossed out leaves a person running on pressure alone. The whole list keeps the aim honest.
cells.sheetLine: The finish is being demanded before the beginning is allowed to start.

cells.tense: You were pointed somewhere once, and the door you walked through is behind you now.
cells.act: look at the whole of it until nothing is left to see
cells.ask: Spread the parts of something you left unfinished across a table, all of them at once, and look without starting, fixing, or planning. Sit there until you've taken in the whole of what's there.
cells.core:
Your direction was real once, and it's gone quiet. Energy still moves toward things, but the effort doesn't land anywhere you can name, and the starts you make stay short. What you were pointed toward sits on the far side of a door you already closed, and you've been standing at the near side of it, looking at the wood.

Nothing here needs to be pushed forward — leaning on a place that has gone quiet only spends what's left. Spread the parts of something you left unfinished across a table and look until the whole of it has been taken in. Seeing it whole comes back first. Motion can wait its turn.

cells.tense: The line is in the pen you are holding, and your account says it is someone else's.
cells.act: lay every piece of it out where you can see all of it at once
cells.ask: Keep a short entry each day for a week. Note what your effort actually moved, plainly, a line or two — what you did, not what it meant. Read the entries back at the end.
cells.core:
Momentum moves through your hands, and whenever it comes up, the credit slides off to circumstance or to a push from somewhere else. The aim is steady underneath, but the account is off by a step. The path gets treated as terrain that was found rather than as a line you are holding, and nothing gives anyone reason to correct it.

What fixes this is smaller than a correction speech. Each day for a week, when effort in you moves something, note it plainly in a line or two — what you did, not what it meant. Read the entries back at the end. A record of small moves returns the ownership that talk kept skipping.
cells.sheetLine: Your hands keep moving and the credit keeps going elsewhere.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim: that the person's drive is a seed held before investment — the record supports seed/potential as the card's face, but I cannot know what the resource in their hand is, so the cells keep the mechanism and leave the object unnamed. The reader could reasonably say this reads their pace rather than their situation, since nothing in the cells names what they're driving toward; the cells name only how the drive is held, which is what the map actually supports. The asks survive a wrong read: each is an ordinary act of sharing support, letting a feeling speak in full, or naming what is on the page, useful even if my locating of the status is off. The sentence that likely serves me more than them: 'the seed of what will be built' — too close to the record's phrasing; it is not said on glass. I keep the asks to the listed acts: give a concrete piece of help and finish it; name every feeling in it on one page, none of them crossed out; lay every piece of it out where you can see all of it at once, twice written two ways so the two Reduction cells do not repeat each other.
